content:
President Donald Trump on Sunday again blamed vandalism for maintenance issues at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, while making a stunning admission about the evidence supporting his claim.

Or rather, the lack of evidence.

Trump wrote on Truth Social on Sunday: "The Reflecting Pool has, in fact, been damaged badly elsewhere, but, unfortunately, there is no video or other evidence, besides the damage itself."

Trump has not only blamed vandals for the alleged damage to the Reflecting Pool, but has also repeatedly insisted he has evidence.

Trump has made similar claims in the past, including in June.

He told reporters at the time: "We have pictures too."

When pressed to produce these images, he said the evidence would be released later.

Last week, Trump was extremely displeased with former Fox News anchor and current Washington D.C. federal prosecutor Jeanine Pirro, because Pirro dropped criminal charges against former Olympic athlete David Hearn, who had been accused of damaging the Reflecting Pool.

Hearn has maintained his innocence, and Pirro issued a statement last week acknowledging that the damage was due to installation errors, not vandalism.

However, Trump insisted in his Sunday post that a "very credible" witness working for the National Park Service saw Hearn "violently" tear up a "rather fragile" surface layer.

This claim also contradicts Trump's previous statements on the matter.

For example, in May of this year, Trump claimed the inner lining was "very strong, very tough," saying it could not be cut even with a knife. He had even driven a motorcade across the pool to inspect the work during construction.

Trump acknowledged that "there were indeed some contractor mistakes," but emphasized that the impact was "relatively minor."

Trump ordered the Reflecting Pool renovated this spring, hoping to complete the repairs in time for the summer Independence Day celebrations. However, problems arose almost immediately. In addition to the lining coming loose and peeling off, the pool water turned green from algae within just a few days of reopening.

He said on Sunday that the Reflecting Pool would reopen "in the near future."
